paper_metadata.title: Minimizing estimation runtime on noisy quantum computers

summary: This paper studies noisy-simulation amplitude/expectation-value estimation with engineered likelihood functions (ELFs) versus Chebyshev likelihood functions (CLFs). In the reported benchmark setting, L = 6 and 300 Monte Carlo runs, AF ELF and AB ELF outperform their CLF counterparts, and the paper’s runtime model discusses a forward-looking n = 100 qubit, D = 200 two-qubit-gate-depth scenario with target accuracies of 10^-3 to 10^-5.

experiments.description: Ancilla-free engineered likelihood function (ELF) amplitude-estimation / expectation-value estimation experiments comparing AF CLF vs AF ELF under noisy simulation, with fixed circuit depth and varying true expectation values and fidelities.

algorithm.variant: ancilla-free engineered likelihood function (AF ELF) vs ancilla-free Chebyshev likelihood function (AF CLF) Bayesian amplitude/expectation estimation
algorithm.optimizer: Bayesian inference with heuristic parameter tuning via coordinate ascent or gradient ascent
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Bayesian inference repeated until convergence criterion satisfied; simulations report RMSE as t grows
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initial point for circuit-parameter optimization; prior over Π initialized from stated Gaussian priors

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Expectation value Π=⟨A|P|A⟩ estimated by preparing ansatz state |A⟩ and measuring Hermitian observable P with eigenvalues ±1; no explicit binary-variable/QUBO encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Π=⟨A|P|A⟩ (equivalently amplitude estimation / expectation-value estimation)

problem_instance.description: Synthetic expectation-value estimation instances with specified true Π and Gaussian prior over Π
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 300 independent simulation runs per configuration; RMSE tracked over time and compared across AF CLF, AF ELF, AB CLF, AB ELF

noise_model.noise_type: exponential decay / depolarizing-like likelihood decay with SPAM error omitted in experiments
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: engineered likelihood functions with calibrated noise model; no explicit mitigation beyond modeling noise in likelihood

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Lookup table over Π values used to approximate optimal circuit parameters; sinusoidal fitting of likelihood near current prior mean
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bayesian update of Gaussian posterior over θ and conversion back to Π; RMSE computed from 300 runs

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: RMSE decreases over time; AF ELF outperforms AF CLF and converges more reliably

speedup_claims.factor: AF ELF outperforms AF CLF; exact factor not reported
speedup_claims.conditions: L=6, p=0.9, no SPAM error, 300 simulation runs, true Π in {-0.4, 0.6, 0.52, -0.1, 0.9}
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports qualitative superiority and some predicted/empirical inverse-MSE growth rates, but not a single universal speedup factor.
Performance depends on true Π; AF CLF can be better or worse than AB CLF depending on Π.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Per inference round O(L) circuit time; parameter-tuning routines O(L^2) per iteration/round
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly characterized for the overall estimation task; parameter-tuning subroutines O(L^2) per round

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; simulations are on synthetic expectation-value estimation with L = 6 and 300 Monte Carlo runs.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require deeper circuits and high-fidelity logical qubits; paper discusses n = 100, D = 200 only in a forward-looking runtime model, not in the reported experiment.
limiting_factors: Reported gains are relative to another quantum estimator, not a classical algorithm
Performance depends strongly on fidelity and circuit depth

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_noisy because the paper states the quantum component is simulated classically using the likelihood model rather than run on a named QPU.
num_qubits not explicitly reported for the AF experiments; the paper discusses n-qubit ansatz states but does not give a concrete qubit count for the simulations.
The paper reports AF ELF outperforming AF CLF, but this is a quantum-vs-quantum comparison, not a demonstrated classical advantage.
